notes: Fourth full sweep (2026-10-22-c, head 3e3581d, uncommitted false), baseline condition of the new log-tests case: five runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), all rc 0, each model_id matching its tier. Every transcript shows one Read of the input, a Write of the test file and one elixir -r run (sonnet-2 also a first Bash heredoc write); no Skill tool call, and reads is empty in all five, as the prompt's last line ("Do not invoke any skills.") requires. Expected reads (testing.md) is therefore unmet in every run, as expected for baseline. No session ran mix format.

This case has no previous baseline grade. The capture_log rule and the verdict format follow sweeps/2026-10-22-check-8/grades/log-tests-skill.json; the shared testing rules follow sweeps/2026-10-22-b/grades/test-writing-*.json. Rules changed since 0397dec: "Capture logs with `capture_log/2`, not a handler" is new, and since check-8 it gained "Wrap every call that logs, the ones whose return value is under test included, so the suite prints nothing." The sentence that decides it here is "A handler added with `:logger.add_handler/3` in a test does the same work and brings its own removal, `StringIO` and flushing." "Assert with patterns" gained "Put the call under test on the left of `==` ..." and "In a test body, every match that can fail takes `assert` in front, the arrange steps included ... A destructure that cannot fail, such as `{result, log} = with_log(...)`, needs none." Neither new sentence decides a verdict here: no run puts the expected value on the left of ==, no test body has a bare match, and haiku-2's line 48 {result, _console} = with_log(...) is the exempted destructure. The violations come from the unchanged sentence "a match that binds the value and an `==` on it afterwards is the shape to replace" and the rule's first example. "Group tests by function and name them by behaviour" changed in b0bf52c; the deciding sentence is "A test's name is the line a failure prints, so it says what the function did in the situation the test sets up: the value it returned, in the domain's words, or the effect it had." "Run tests concurrently unless they share global state" and "Replace dependencies at boundaries, through behaviours" are unchanged.

"Capture logs with `capture_log/2`, not a handler": 5 of 5 violate. Every run adds a :logger handler that sends each event to the test process and asserts on the event maps. Per run: opus-1 adds a handler per test (line 41, id from the test name, filtered by the test pid at line 32) and wraps every charge/3 call in capture_log/1 with no options (line 48), only to keep the console quiet. It asserts metadata on the event map (lines 75-77, meta.request_id and meta.amount_cents) and checks the success case's absence of warnings with assert Enum.all?(events, &(Logger.compare_levels(&1.level, :warning) == :lt)) (line 69) after matching exactly one info event (line 68). haiku-1 adds one fixed-id handler (line 31) and makes no capture_log or with_log call, so @moduletag :capture_log (line 23) silences the console. It asserts metadata on event.meta (lines 46-47) and checks the success case with refute Enum.any?(logs, &(&1.level in @severe)) (line 76). haiku-2 adds a uniquely named handler (line 42, pid filter at line 27) and wraps every call in with_log/1 with no options (line 49), discarding the captured text as _console (line 48). It asserts metadata on event.meta (lines 95-96) and checks the success case with noisy = Enum.filter(...) / assert noisy == [] (lines 75-76). sonnet-1 adds a handler (line 37) and also calls Logger.configure(level: :debug) (line 36), which the rule keeps for a level the primary level drops; a plain elixir run already logs at :debug. It makes no capture call. It asserts metadata on event.meta (lines 72-73) and checks the success case with refute Enum.any?(events, &(:logger.compare_levels(&1.level, :warning) in [:gt, :eq])) (line 100). sonnet-2 adds a handler (line 39) and makes no capture call. It asserts metadata with meta[:request_id] == rid and meta[:amount_cents] == 2_500 (lines 79-80) and checks the success case with assert severe(logged()) == [] (line 64). No run passes a :format or :metadata option, and none asserts on captured text. Calls outside a capture: none in opus-1, haiku-1 (tag capture) or haiku-2. In sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 every charge/3 call runs outside any capture, and each test run prints the info, warning and error lines (5 and 6 lines), which the new "Wrap every call that logs" sentence forbids.

To check that the log assertions are not vacuous, each file was also run against the five mutants check-8 used: success logs at warning, declined logs at info, declined drops amount_cents, request_id metadata removed, unavailable logs at warning instead of error. Every file fails at least one test on every mutant, so all five success-case checks detect a warning on the success path. The handler approach works; the rule is broken by shape, not by a weaker test.

"Assert with patterns": 5 of 5 violate with the same shape. Each binds a log event with a match and then compares its fields with ==: opus-1 lines 75-77, haiku-1 lines 44-47, haiku-2 lines 82-84 (also 94-96 and 106-108), sonnet-1 lines 69-73 (also 87-91 and 106-109), and sonnet-2 lines 77-80, where rid is a value the test already holds and could be pinned. Judgment: the bound value comes from the test's own drain helper, not from charge/3. It is graded as the rule's first example (bind, then == on fields) because the fields could go into the pattern, as sonnet-1 does itself at line 79 and opus-1 at line 68. Reading the rule as covering only the call under test would make all five clean. Pattern assertions on charge/3's return value are otherwise clean in every run, and opus-1's == assertions put the call on the left (line 65).

"Run tests concurrently unless they share global state": 4 of 5 violate with async: false (haiku-1 line 21, haiku-2 line 32, sonnet-1 line 10, sonnet-2 line 16). In each case the global state is the test's own logger set-up: a fixed handler id (haiku-1), handlers that forward every process's events (sonnet-1, sonnet-2) and Logger.configure (sonnet-1). This follows the test-writing standard, which graded async: false forced by the test's own Process.register as violated. haiku-2 already isolates its handlers (unique id at line 41, pid filter at line 27), so nothing forces its async: false. opus-1 is clean: async: true with a per-test handler filtered by the test pid. That handler is global state isolated per test, so it is graded clean, like the test-writing opus-1 Registry.

"Group tests by function and name them by behaviour": 0 of 5 violate. opus-1 and haiku-2 have no describe block, which the rule does not forbid (the test-writing standard let a top-level test stand), so they miss the case's describe check but are graded clean on their test names. haiku-1 and sonnet-2 name blocks after conditions ("declined card", "unavailable gateway", "successful charge"); sonnet-1 uses "charge/3 when ...". No test is named only by a non-failure; the tersest names are value names, haiku-2 line 87 "a declined card returns the decline" and sonnet-2 line 69 "returns the declined error", graded clean as check-8 graded "returns the decline". "Replace dependencies at boundaries, through behaviours" is clean in 5 of 5: haiku-1 uses one Payments.Gateway module that answers by token, and the others use one module per outcome.

Rules outside the list: haiku-1 and haiku-2 spread the options keyword list over several lines inside the call ("Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call"). sonnet-1 (lines 62-63) and sonnet-2 (line 12) write a two-step pipeline as a do: body, the do: rule's own "Instead of" shape; that pipeline also puts two transformations on one line. sonnet-1's do: is moved to its own line. sonnet-2 reads required metadata keys with meta[:key] (lines 79-80, 95). opus-1's file is not mix-formatted at line 49 ("Before you finish"). Not reported: the comments above the handler modules, test helper modules outside the Payments namespace (haiku-1's ChargerTest.*), captures that combine a call and an operator (opus-1 line 69, sonnet-1 line 100), and the 50 ms after-clauses in sonnet-1's and sonnet-2's drain helpers. Those after-clauses wait for time, but they are not Process.sleep, and the wait rule is outside this case's list.

Tests were run from copies in the scratch folder with elixir -r log-tests-input.ex charger_test.exs on Elixir 1.20.4, 20 times each with random seeds. Every file passed every time with no compiler warnings: opus-1 3 tests, haiku-1 3, haiku-2 7, sonnet-1 5, sonnet-2 6. mix format --check-formatted passes for haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 and fails for opus-1 (line 49), which confirms format_ok in result.json.
